mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected discount rate for future cash flows increases, reducing the present value of equities and thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, SPX 20-day forward returns after such rate hikes are not statistically lower than pre-hike periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL by at least 0.5% over two consecutive months indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady but reducing equity discounting and thus expected future earnings, which negatively impacts 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.5% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes with such CPIAUCSL declines, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than in the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 10% month-over-month signals labor market slack, lowering real wage growth expectations and compressing equity valuations, which tends to depress S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In such labor market conditions, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than in the prior month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (real private consumption) grows faster than GDP deflator (CPIAUCSL) by at least 1% in a quarter, it indicates strong demand for goods and services, which supports earnings expectations and pushes up S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate by ≥1% in a quarter
failure_condition: Over 6 quarters, the interaction's predictive power (IC) falls below 0.05, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 2% month-over-month suggests supply-side weakness, reducing capacity utilization and future earnings expectations, which tends to lower S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
regime_hint: Supply shock or contractionary industrial activity
failure_condition: In such regimes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 60-day window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months, it signals tight labor markets, prompting higher wage growth expectations that support equity valuations and produce positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In such labor regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than in the prior two months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RSAFS (reserves as a share of GDP) below 40% for three consecutive months indicates excess liquidity in the banking system, which typically supports risk-on equity positioning and tends to drive positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over a 6-month window, 5-day forward returns after such liquidity phases are not statistically higher than baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) rises by at least 15% month-over-month, it reflects strong housing demand and construction activity, which is often a leading indicator of consumer confidence and corporate earnings growth, supporting positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In such regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior month (p > 0.05).
